subject: Critical Thinking
title: Inversion: Solving Problems Backwards
description: A quick win: understand Inversion: Solving Problems Backwards.

hook.text: Charlie Munger's advice: 'Invert, always invert.' Instead of asking how to succeed, ask: how would I guarantee failure?

buildup.text: Inversion: instead of solving for the best outcome, identify and avoid the worst ones.

discovery.text: Carl Jacobi, the mathematician, solved hard problems by working backwards. Munger applied this to investing and life.

twist.text: 'How do I build a great company?' is hard.

climax.text: Inversion works because failure modes are more predictable than success paths.

punchline.text: Don't just plan to win. Plan to not lose.

quiz.question: What is the inversion thinking technique?
options: Solving problems by identifying and avoiding the worst outcomes

details.summary: Inversion approaches problems by asking what you want to avoid rather than what you want to achieve. Instead of asking how to succeed, ask what guarantees failure and avoid that. Charlie Munger credits inversion as his most powerful mental model.
details.whyItMatters: Inversion reveals risks and obstacles that forward thinking misses because avoidable failures are often more identifiable than specific paths to success.
takeaways: Avoiding stupidity is often easier than achieving brilliance
Inversion surfaces risks that forward planning overlooks
Charlie Munger and Carl Jacobi both advocated inverting problems

faq.question: How do you apply inversion to a business strategy problem?
faq.answer: Instead of asking 'How do we grow revenue?' ask 'What would guarantee we lose all our customers?' Then make sure you are not doing any of those things. Preventing certain failure is clearer than engineering uncertain success.

faq.question: Why does inversion work when forward thinking sometimes fails?
faq.answer: Success can happen many ways, making it hard to plan for. Failure patterns are fewer and more predictable. By identifying and eliminating failure modes, you increase the probability of success without needing to predict its exact form.
